summary: Presence analytics now derives real routes: a ground-truth speed computed from consecutive fixes (never Life360's own mostly-empty speed field), named corridors that accumulate across cycles from the road-name sequences Life360 already sends, and per-corridor speed percentiles by hour-of-week — a congestion model built entirely from a subject's own history.
details: New tables presence_trips, presence_corridors, presence_corridor_speed (migration 0019), plus presence_trips.sequence (migration 0020).
A trip is the movement between two confirmed stays; a corridor is a named cluster of trips whose road-name sequences are close by edit distance.

Corridors accumulate over time rather than needing a burst: each trip's own road-name sequence is stored, and a trip stays in the clustering pool until it is linked, so three occurrences of a daily commute on three different days name the route just as well as three in one batch. The clustering pass is bounded by a new measured knob, analytics.corridor_cluster_batch_limit (default 500).

Corridor identity is a durable id, preserved across re-clustering the same way Tier 3's place identity fix established — a corridor does not churn a new id every cycle — and two equidistant corridors now resolve to the lower id in both storage backends instead of whichever the database happened to return first.
nora_analytics_corridors_total gained an outcome label (created/reconfirmed), so a corridor being BORN is visible in metrics rather than indistinguishable from one being re-seen.

An address-less trip can never mint or contaminate a corridor: the clustering pool excludes trips with no road names at all, because an empty road-name sequence is a similarity-neighbour of nearly any short real corridor under edit distance.
limitations: A trip's still-ambiguous tail (has not yet resolved into a closed stay or continued movement) is never extracted early — a small sliver at that exact seam is accepted as lost, not guessed.
Corridor and speed-percentile data has no consumer yet, matching Tier 3's own posture — nothing reads presence_trips/presence_corridors/presence_corridor_speed outside this substrate today.

Trip extraction has no analogous protection to a stay's own settled_seconds withholding of an open stay: the analytics tick (nora/analytics/__main__.py's _tick) fires on cadence alone and does not yet implement DEC-115's three fire conditions (safety_lag backlog, settled_seconds quiet boundary, max_age_seconds), a pre-existing gap from Tier 1 that Tier 5 inherits rather than introduces. Under real driving conditions this can fragment one continuous trip into several short trips, and at corridor_max_edit_distance=2 over the resulting short road-name sequences, genuinely distinct routes can collapse into one corridor. Corridors themselves do form and grow correctly; what this gap affects is the quality of the trip boundaries feeding them — a separate, not-yet-made design decision.
